page: Amazon Web Services c8in.4xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features a dedicated x86_64 Intel processor operating at a 3.9 GHz clock speed. The configuration provides 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, allowing two threads per core.

System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions such as Amazon Elastic Block Store for all persistent data operations. It does not contain GPU hardware accelerators.

Networking capabilities are defined by a 25 Gbps baseline bandwidth allocation, aligning with the network-optimized focus of the c8in family. The architecture prioritizes CPU clock frequency and network throughput over local disk and high memory density. This resource profile fits network-intensive applications, distributed data processing nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and high-traffic web serving layers.
description: Amazon Web Services c8in.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor running on the AWS Nitro System. Configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores at a 3.9 GHz clock rate, the system delivers compute capacity paired with 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This configuration includes no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, routing persistent storage requirements through network-attached block devices. A key hardware attribute is its 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, supporting intensive network data flow. The resource distribution balances high processor frequencies against moderate memory allocation, establishing high efficiency for CPU-bound tasks requiring significant throughput. Typical workload fits comprise distributed network appliances, high-traffic web servers, video encoding pipelines, batch compute processes, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
